brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor mapping: streak length to bloom stage creates instant emotional read of progress and neglect
Differentiated states (flower, sprout, wilted, empty pot) give each card visceral storytelling at a glance
Playful illustration style matches the nurturing, gentle tone of the habit-as-garden concept
dominant_weaknesses: Saturated green ground vs pale blue header clash; the gradient-to-brown soil muddies the whole canvas
All flowers look identical regardless of habit — wasted opportunity for per-habit plant species or color personality
Cards float awkwardly over plants; typography is generic system sans with no botanical or handcrafted character
fix_priorities: Refine palette: desaturate background, unify header and garden tones into one cohesive natural gradient
Differentiate plants per habit (succulent, fern, sunflower) so the garden reads as a real ecosystem
Upgrade typography to something with warmth/character and tighten card chrome to feel less templated
Add subtle motion hints (sway, water droplet animation) implied by static design language
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral metaphor leads, behavioral loop is clear via Water Today CTA, but reflective depth (history, seasons, growth arc) is shallow.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the bloom/wilt/streak mapping directly embodies the brief, though execution polish lags the concept.
